Hi Sabrina — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the questionnaire; I answered the sections you flagged and attached a short summary + sample evidence. Key points up front:

- Residency: Hosted API data for NovaPulse would be stored in the region you select at signup (we currently support us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). By default, generated outputs and request payloads persist in encrypted object storage in the chosen region. We do not replicate tenant data cross-region unless explicitly configured for DR.

- Retention: Default retention for raw request payloads and generated outputs is 30 days. Cache artifacts (inference KV cache) are ephemeral and typically retained only for the duration of active sessions; embeddings derived via the Redwood API are not stored long-term unless the customer opts into our managed embeddings feature. If a customer uses managed embeddings, retention is configurable and defaults to 90 days.

- Deletion / Tenant wipe: We support a tenant wipe workflow that removes object-store blobs and associated metadata. Typical complete wipe timeline is: enqueue wipe -> delete objects (0–4 hours, dependent on dataset size) -> background metadata and index cleanup (up to 24 hours). We attach a one-page playbook that describes the steps and provides sample audit log lines.

- Audit & Evidence: We attach a redacted audit log sample showing a tenant-delete operation for a previous customer (auditlog-sample-2028-11-22.csv). For compliance reviews, we can provide additional redacted examples or a scoped attestation under NDA. We are SOC 2 Type II and attach a short SOC summary.

See the attached PDF for the questionnaire answers (section numbers mapped to your doc). If you want, I can include a short sample of the API call/response used to trigger a tenant wipe and a redacted audit-log export.

Next steps: If these answers look good, Ben can schedule a short 30-min follow-up to walk procurement through the wipe process and the evidence pack.

Regards,

Thanks, Priyom — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from my team after a quick review:

1) Embeddings: you mentioned managed embeddings default to 90 days. If a customer does NOT opt in to managed embeddings, are there any logs or transient stores that could retain vectorized representations beyond request processing? We need assurance that vectors are not materialized in durable storage.

2) Backup snapshots: do you take backups of object storage which would include tenant objects? If so, what is the retention on those backups and how are they scoped by region/tenant?

3) Audit proof: the sample audit log looks redacted-friendly, but we need a canonical format you produce for tenant-wipe events (fields we typically expect: timestamp, operator/service account, tenant_id, object_count, operation_id). Can you confirm the full set and whether the audit entries are immutable?

If you can answer these three as bullets and include a short timeline for a worst-case full wipe on a 20TB tenant, we should be able to close review.

Best,
Sabrina

Ben / Irene — internal note before I reply to Sabrina's three clarifying bullets:

- Embeddings: confirm again that non-managed runs do not persist vector artifacts. My understanding: our runtime may materialize intermediate tensors in ephemeral instance-attached storage during inference but we never write vectorized embeddings to durable object storage unless the customer explicitly calls the embeddings endpoint that writes to the managed embeddings store. Please confirm so I can state this plainly.

- Backups: we do periodic region-local snapshots for system metadata and long-term backups for operational recovery. For tenant objects (customer blobs), we keep backups for up to 30 days in the same region; backups are encrypted and access-controlled by KMS keys scoped to the region. Need Irene to confirm exact snapshot cadence and whether any cross-region replication is enabled by default (it is not, but we should cite the internal runbook).

- Audit proof format: Irene, can you attach the canonical audit-schema example and the script that extracts a tenant-wipe row (fields: timestamp, service_account, tenant_id, operation_id, object_count, status, checksum) — we'll send a redacted CSV. Also include a line that audit logs are append-only in our ELK pipeline for 90 days and retained per compliance policies after that (we have SOC2 controls that cover immutability for 90 days; long-term retention is in our retention matrix).

I'll reply to Sabrina with short bullets and attach the audit extract and a worst-case timeline estimate for a 20TB tenant (roughly: enqueue -> object delete approx 24–36 hours when throttled to maintain cluster stability; metadata cleanup additional 48 hours; full validation + audit log stabilization up to 72 hours worst-case).

If you can confirm the two technical bits (embeddings persistence and exact snapshot cadence) I will finalize the external reply. Ben — let me know if you'd like to join the follow-up call; Sabrina suggested a 30-min slot next Thursday.

Thanks,
Priyom
